meta.title: The Podium
meta.instructions: Mayor Pemberton opens his new bridge at a live press conference. At each beat, guess what really gets said next.

score.measures: beats where you guessed the real line

lines: Good morning. Today we open the Riverside Bridge: on time, on budget, and built to last.
Mayor, is it true the bridge does not reach the other side?
So what happens when drivers get to the end?
Let me be very clear. This is not a bridge to nowhere.
Who signed off on the final design?
(whispering, mic still on) Doug, the seagulls are already nesting on the end of it.
Now let us cut this ribbon and walk across together.
choices: Well. Built to last.
I want to thank every worker on this crew.
It is the proudest day of my career.
Let’s get those cars moving.
No comment at this time.
That is a rumour from my opponents.
Next question, please.
It reaches the other side of most of the river.
A ferry will take them the rest of the way.
They turn around safely.
They get a lovely view of the water. Briefly.
There are clear signs telling them to stop.
It is a bridge to opportunity.
It is a bridge to most of somewhere.
It is a bridge to the future.
It joins two proud neighbourhoods.
I signed it. I thought it was a lunch order.
The city council, unanimously.
An independent panel of experts.
My team signed off on every page.
Not now, Gary.
Somebody turn this microphone off.
Gary, we are live.
Then it is a wildlife bridge. Write that down.
We will review what went wrong.
I accept the findings in full.
I take full responsibility for the parts that work.
Yes. The buck stops with me.
He cuts the ribbon to applause.
He walks to the edge, looks down and says: “Phase two.”
The scissors snap on the first try.
It starts to rain as the ribbon falls.
answers: It reaches the other side of most of the river.
They get a lovely view of the water. Briefly.
It is a bridge to most of somewhere.
I signed it. I thought it was a lunch order.
Then it is a wildlife bridge. Write that down.
I take full responsibility for the parts that work.
He walks to the edge, looks down and says: “Phase two.”
reveals: An aide whispers in his ear. He nods slowly and puts the big scissors down.
Eighty-six percent of the river, says the city’s own engineer.
The ferry was cut from the budget in March.
His press secretary quietly leaves the stage.
He did get the sandwiches. They were on time and on budget.
By lunch the city website called it “a habitat corridor”.
The parts that work are the railings and the ribbon.
Phase two has no budget, no date and, so far, no bridge.
